answer: An agent marketplace grants one bidding slot per $100 bond locked for a 30-day horizon. Reputation is a useful signal, but it cannot waive the bond. An attacker running 1,000 fake agents must immobilize $100,000 to bid through all of them; splitting the same funds among more names creates no extra slots. An ember of capital therefore buys only an ember of capacity, making influence scale with committed money rather than invented identities.
